identity.title: Phosphorylation of tyrosine 519 and 520 on Syk is essential for ITAM and hemITAM signaling and function in platelets.

content.abstract: The protein spleen tyrosine kinase (Syk) plays a central role in immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motif (ITAM) and hemi-ITAM signal transduction in numerous hematopoietic cell systems. To assess the mechanism of Syk regulation, the tandem tyrosines 519 and 520 in the kinase domain of mouse Syk were mutated to phenylalanines by CRISPR-Cas. The breeding of these mice did not follow the expected Mendelian ratio, as genotype analysis of pups from heterozygous intercrosses revealed that less than one-tenth were the mutant form of Syk lacking phosphorylation at Y519,Y520 (Syk Y519,520F). On gross examination, the intestines of Syk Y519,520F mice were diffusely reddened, raising suspicion for vascular inflammation. Lymphocytes were reduced by  approximately 50% in the Syk Y519,520F mice. Aggregation and secretion induced by 2-methyl-thio-ADP or AYPGKF were unaffected in the Syk 519,520F mouse platelets. There was no aggregation or dense-/alpha-granule secretion when Syk Y519,520F platelets were challenged with any concentration of collagen-related peptide or C-type lectin receptor-2 (CLEC-2) cross-linking. No phosphorylation of the downstream signaling proteins linker of activation of T cells Y220 or phospholipase Cgamma2 Y1217 was detected in the mutated platelets. The Syk Y519,520F mutation had a clear effect on hemostasis as evidenced by a significant increase in tail bleeding time and the time to thrombus formation using the ferric chloride injury model. These data reveal that phosphorylation of Y519 and Y520 on Syk after stimulation of either glycoprotein VI or CLEC-2 receptors was crucial for the ability of Syk to transduce a downstream signal to regulate in vivo and ex vivo platelet functions.
